title: The Effect of BST via Telehealth on Caregiver Implementation of Incidental Teaching
abstract: The increasing prevalence of autism spectrum disorder has increased the need for accessible and scalable behavioral health services. Incidental teaching is an effective naturalistic intervention for increasing communication skills in children with autism, and behavior skills training is an effective method for teaching caregivers to implement evidence-based practices. Although telehealth has emerged as a viable modality for caregiver training, additional replications are needed. This study replicated and extended prior research by evaluating BST delivered via telehealth to train caregivers to implement incidental teaching. Nine caregiver child dyads and three trainers participated. Trainers used synchronous videoconferencing, and researchers evaluated outcomes using three multiple baseline single case designs. Following training, all caregivers improved procedural fidelity and reached 100% accuracy across two consecutive sessions. Caregivers also increased communication opportunities, resulting in increased child mands above baseline levels. Findings support telehealth delivered BST as an effective model for caregiver training.
